F1.evidence: Hydration owner label `sessions.transcript-hydration.*` (session-transcript.worker.ts:664 via withHistoryDatabase) enables statement timing at sqlite-transaction.ts:473-481, but on SQLite the read-only scope opens via openSqliteReadOnlyDatabase -> openNodeSqliteDatabase (openclaw-agent-db-readonly-open.ts:173, node-sqlite.ts:73) and never calls observeConnection, which is the only SQLite feeder of statementTiming (observation.ts:216-283; only open.ts:91 / adapters.ts:35 call it). A slow hold therefore logs statementExecutionMs 0 and an empty summary; log-only diagnostic.

F2.evidence: session-accessor.sqlite-active-context.ts:475-541 does materialize every custom/context-ineligible candidate's navigation (CASE at :458-462 projects custom events) before the outer predicates, where the old query filtered before sorting. Whether this actually exhausts temp storage depends on a non-default PostgreSQL temp_file_limit, work_mem and history sizes, which the code cannot settle.

F3.evidence: sqlite-transaction.ts:480-481 calls startSqliteStatementTiming(true) for every hydration-owned transaction, and observation.ts:22-29/66-71 calls observeGcSamples and its stop, which in gc-observer.ts:93-123 either creates a GCProfiler+interval or runs drain(true) (profiler stop/start and subscriber fan-out) at both ends regardless of slowness. The overhead is real but small per transaction and not shown to be user-noticeable.
